scenes.headline: drop()
scenes.subtitle: Removing columns you no longer need.
scenes.narration: The drop transformation removes one or more columns, producing a slimmer DataFrame.

scenes.headline: What drop does
items: Removes named columns from the DataFrame
Silently ignores column names that do not exist
Returns a new DataFrame with the rest intact
Useful for hiding sensitive or redundant fields
scenes.narration: Drop removes the named columns from a DataFrame and quietly ignores names that do not exist. It returns a new DataFrame with the remaining columns intact, which is handy for hiding sensitive or redundant fields.

scenes.headline: Dropping a sensitive column
scenes.code:
safe_df = user_data_df.drop("password_hash")

# Drop several at once
slim_df = user_data_df.drop("password_hash", "ssn")
scenes.narration: First we drop the password hash column to produce a safe DataFrame. Then we show that drop accepts several column names at once, removing both the password hash and the social security number in a single call.

scenes.text: drop is the mirror of select — use whichever expresses your intent most clearly.
scenes.narration: Drop is the mirror image of select, so use whichever one expresses your intent most clearly for the columns involved.
